summary: The bill amends the Foreign Agents Registration Act to require that informational materials distributed by agents include a conspicuous statement disclosing whether their foreign principal is supervised, directed, owned, controlled, financed, or subsidized by China, Russia, North Korea, Iran, or governments acting on their behalf.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends disclosure requirements under the Foreign Agents Registration Act but contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations. It imposes no new costs or savings on the government.
The legislation addresses only informational disclosure obligations for foreign agents and has no connection to tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
No provisions in the bill relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public health programs, or market structures in the healthcare sector.
The bill is silent on firearms, gun ownership, or regulatory measures concerning weapons.
While the bill references foreign principals and covered nations, it does not alter immigration pathways, visas, border enforcement, or protections for noncitizens.
The legislation contains no language concerning reproductive rights, abortion access, or related healthcare regulations.

The bill references the statutory definition of 'covered nation' from title 10 of the U.S. Code (defense-related), but this is merely definitional and does not affect military budgets, force structure, or defense policy.
No environmental, energy, or climate-related provisions appear in the bill.
The bill does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social assistance policies.
No provisions concern schools, federal education funding, curriculum, or school choice.
The legislation has no bearing on drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
While the bill amends a registration statute enforced by the Department of Justice, it does not modify criminal penalties, sentencing, or policing practices.
The bill addresses foreign influence and propaganda disclosures rather than tariffs, trade agreements, import restrictions, or globalization measures.
No fiscal or deficit-related provisions are present.
The bill contains no language regarding legal protections or restrictions based on sexual orientation or gender identity.
The legislation does not authorize, modify, or restrict any foreign assistance programs.

Although the bill aims to increase transparency around foreign propaganda that could influence public discourse, it does not alter voting procedures, election administration, voter access, or campaign finance rules.
The bill requires additional disclosures on informational materials but imposes no new data-protection mandates, platform regulations, or privacy standards.
No provisions address collective bargaining, worker protections, or union governance.
The legislation does not engage with religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination rules.
